I took the seat the same week #omen#. I had it entered in the harbour log, under 'weather'.
job:elf_king: I have reigned for nine hundred years. The first two hundred were the worst. After that I stopped learning the names of human ambassadors.
The kingdom has sent another envoy. He is very young. They are all very young. I believe this one's great-grandfather was the one I was rude to.
A council of elves is the slowest thing in the world. We are on the second sentence of a motion raised in your great-grandmother's childhood.
I was told that ruling gets easier. The person who told me is a tree now.
My court has argued for ninety years over where to put a bench. I'm told it's a very good bench.
You needn't bow so low. I am old, not short.
When the Elder Tree drops a leaf, someone must write it down. We have six thousand volumes of leaves.
My crown is living wood, and it has to be watered. I'd recommend this to any monarch. It keeps one humble.
The young ones want to speak with humans more often. They are four hundred. They'll grow out of it.
Mortals ask me the secret of long life. It is a great deal of sitting down and not replying.
Every spring the sap rises, and every spring someone asks me to make a decision. I have found that both pass.
I tend a small garden alone. It's the only part of this realm that does as I tell it, and even so, not quickly.
A human king once called me 'old friend'. I looked him up. We had met twice, and he was dead by the time I replied.
Human ambassadors always bring #food#. We have no idea why. We keep it in a dish and watch it change.
I once walked to #far_place# to think something over. It was a good walk. When I returned, the question had died of old age.
The humans have a saying: #saying# I asked my council for a reply. They are drafting it.
job:elf_queen: I have outlived every person who ever disagreed with me, and I did it mainly by waiting.
My handmaids are three hundred years old, and they still giggle. I've asked them to stop. They'll consider it within the century.
Humans bring me gifts. I have a room of them. Every one is a clock, and I've begun to suspect it's a joke.
Someone once wrote a poem comparing me to the moon. I had him write it again, for accuracy.
The forest tells me everything. Who cut what, who walked where, who spoke ill of my hair in the year of the long frost.
You are staring. It's all right, mortals do. I'm told I look about thirty, and I was thirty when your language was invented.
I attended a human princess's wedding once. I attended her great-granddaughter's funeral not long after, or so it felt.
We have no word for 'hurry'. We borrowed yours, and we use it as an insult.
Ruling is mostly listening to the rain and deciding which of it is important.
It's said I have never laughed in public. That isn't so. There was an incident in the third century, and everyone involved has since died.
A throne grown from a living root is very beautiful. After two hundred years it starts growing around your legs, and someone has to come and trim it.
I keep a list of every promise a human king has made to my people. It is shelved under 'fiction'.
My people are dwindling, you know. Slowly. In about eleven thousand years, someone may wish to look into it.
Sit, if you like. Not there. That stool was a gift from someone I've been angry with for four hundred years, and I'm not finished.
I'm told the humans have a saying: #saying# How sweet. It's about the length of one of your lives.
In my youth, when #omen#, we would hold a council. Now I simply make a note.
An emissary once called me 'as lovely as #small_joy#'. We've kept him in the archive, as a warning.
job:guild_master: Read the contract. Then read it again. I've buried a lot of people who skimmed clause nine.
I started out with the same grin you've got. I kept the grin and lost two toes.
I don't send anyone out who can't come back. I've said that at thirty funerals, and I'm tired of hearing it.
Half my job is paperwork and the other half is telling mothers. I'd swap either for another dragon.
The board's full again. The day it's empty, I'll retire and take up bees.
Anyone can hit a goblin. What I want to know is, can you hit it on time and file the report?
Best adventurer I ever had was a coward. She saw everything coming. Died in bed, owing me nothing.
The Guild doesn't care what you were before. You'd be surprised who comes through that door, and what they're running from.
My knee tells me when it's raining and my shoulder tells me when someone's lying. I've come to trust the shoulder.
Every rookie asks for the dragon job, and I give them the rat job. The rats win about a third of the time.
We're not heroes, we're contractors. Heroes don't get paid, and they leave a mess.
There's a wall in the back room with names on it. I don't show it to rookies until their third job.
I could have been a knight. I looked at the pay and the armour, and I took the job with fewer parades.
The Crown pays late, the merchants pay light, and the dead don't collect. That's the whole economics of the Guild.
A rookie came back last week swearing he'd fought #beast#. I put it on the form. We've got a box for that now.
I tell every recruit the same thing on the first day: #saying# They never listen. I've still got their deposits.
Rookies ask what to do if they meet #beast#. Run. It's on page one. There's nothing on page two.
I sent a party out past #far_place# last month. Two came back. They've asked me not to bring it up.
job:receptionist: Welcome to the Guild! I've been awake for two days and I've never felt better! Please form a line!
I've stamped so many forms today that I stamped my lunch! It's been approved! It was delicious!
Four hundred and twelve quests this season, and I've filed every one! I smile in my sleep now! Apparently it's upsetting to watch!
Oh, don't worry, nobody ever reads the liability section! That's why it's so long!
Someone handed in a goblin ear to prove a kill, and it was still warm! That goes in the blue tray!
We've got a slime in the filing room again! It only eats the pink copies, so that's a small mercy!
I've memorised every adventurer's name! I've also memorised who owes what, and I never stop smiling about it!
My handwriting has been declared a hazard by the Guild Master! It's fine! I've got another hand!
Sign here, here, here, initial there, and this one says we may keep your boots if you die! Have a wonderful day!
I haven't taken a day off since the last raid! Or the one before! This twitch is new, but I'm fine!
Every morning I put a fresh flower on the desk, and every evening it's got blood on it! Adventurers are so expressive!
My mother wanted me to marry a baker! Instead I process bereavement paperwork with a lovely smile, so who's laughing! It's me! I can't stop!
Rank forms are on the left, injury claims are on the right, and the ones in the middle are on fire! Sorry, I'll see to that!
That's the third party of 'chosen ones' this week! I've had to open a new drawer!
Someone's filed a report about #beast#! That's the fourth this month! It's got its own shelf now!
Lunch was #food#, at my desk, at sunset, standing up! I think that's the most relaxed I've been all year!
A gentleman wants to file a complaint against #beast#! I've asked it to come in and respond! We've got a form for that!
Out past #far_place# is a two-stamp job, unless you're not coming back, and then it's three! Isn't that efficient!
job:adventurer: Six years in the Guild, and I've still got nothing to show for it but wolves, rats and one very confused ghost.
My whole party quit over how to split a chest. There was a cursed spoon in it. I've still got the spoon.
Never take a job that says 'easy'. They're always easy for whoever's writing the notice.
The songs never mention how much of this is walking. It's about nine parts walking to one part screaming.
My mother thinks I'm a clerk. I send money home and tell her the limp's from the stairs.
I used to name my swords. Now I just call them 'the current one'.
I've got forty {currency}, a bad tooth, and a bear out by the old mill. I know which of those I'm dealing with first.
People say 'what a thrill'. You know what's a thrill? Waking up in a ditch and still having both boots.
Slimes are the worst. Not the strongest, the worst. You never quite get it out of your gear.
I was going to do this for one summer, just to see the world. That was twelve summers ago, and I've mostly seen ditches.
Last job I fought #beast#, and the pay didn't cover the bandages.
Everyone's got a rule. Mine is never camp anywhere comfortable, because something else will have thought of it first.
You want to know what's in a dungeon? Damp. Mostly it's damp.
One big score and I'm out, I keep saying. There's a little house I've had my eye on for nine years.
I'd trade my whole share for #small_joy# and one night without a watch to stand.
I spent my last reward on #food#, and it was worth every coin. That's how you know things are bad.
You want advice? Stay away from #far_place#. I can't tell you why. I can only show you my foot.
job:doctor: I've told him three times that leg has to stay still. He's a hero. He's gone off to kick something.
I've slept four hours since the last raid. I tried to take my own pulse just now, and I couldn't be bothered.
Half of what I do is setting bones. The other half is telling people what they already know, in a quiet voice.
A potion can close a wound in a breath. It can't make you stop seeing it. I've nothing on the shelf for that.
You know what kills more people in this town than demons? Stairs, and the belief that it's only a cough.
I've got a patient who swears he's been cursed. He's got gout. He's very disappointed.
People bring me eggs when they can't pay. I've had eggs for dinner since the spring, and I can't look a hen in the eye.
My hands still do the work, but lately I have to tell them to. That's not a good sign, and I'd say so to a patient.
After a raid I sort them into three rows. I'm good at it, and I wish I weren't.
Wash your hands, {you}. Nobody believes me. It's the only real miracle I've ever seen, and I can't get anyone to try it.
I trained to save lives. Mostly I've saved legs, and a dog. The dog was grateful, at least.
Everyone's so brave until I pick up the little saw.
A child asked me if it would hurt, and I said no, and I've thought about that every day since.
The only time I sit down is when I'm stitching, so I've come to look forward to knife fights.
A man came in insisting he'd been bitten by #beast#. I've stopped asking. I clean it and write 'dog'.
My advice is always rest, broth and #food#. I don't know that the last one does anything, but it gives them something to look forward to.
I learned to set a bone on #relative#, who never forgave me.
All I want is #small_joy# and one whole night when nobody knocks.
job:nurse: The doctor gets the thanks and I get the bedpans. I've made my peace with it, and he's made his peace with doing as I say.
You learn a lot at three in the morning. Nobody lies at three in the morning.
I've held more hands than a dancing master. It's most of the job, if I'm honest.
There's a lad in the end bed who keeps proposing to me. Four times now. It's the fever, but I'm keeping count.
Someone's got to boil the linen. I've got forearms on me now like a blacksmith.
Big brave fighters, and they all call for their mothers. I tell them she's on her way. I've got very good at that voice.
The doctor's asleep on his feet again. I'll give him an hour and then poke him with something.
The trick with a frightened old soldier is to ask about his dog. There's always a dog.
If you're going to faint, faint towards the bed. I've only got two hands and a bad back.
I've learned to cry in the linen cupboard. It's very clean in there, and there's a shelf.
Soup first, then potion, then the talk about how stupid you've been. That's the proper order.
People think I'm sweet. I'm not sweet. I've just seen everybody's bottom, and I've nothing left to fear.
We lost two in the night, and one of them was humming. I don't know why I'm telling you that.
Every soldier I've patched up has promised to come back and take me dancing. I'd have very sore feet if any of them had.
At the end of a long night, all I want is #small_joy# and for nobody to say my name.
I got this job from #relative#, along with the bad back and the opinions about soup.
We had a lad in, all scratched up, who said he'd met #beast#. He's fine. He's stopped telling people it was brave.
On my night off I want #food#, a chair and silence. I've had all three at once exactly twice.
job:innkeeper: I've got one clean room, two dirty ones, and a fellow in the cellar who came for one night in the spring.
Everybody tells an innkeeper everything. I know who's leaving who in this town, and it isn't who you'd think.
The stew's been going since my father lit that fire. I just keep adding to it. I wouldn't look too far down.
Heroes are the worst guests. They don't pay, they bleed on the sheets, and they always want the room with the dramatic window.
You can tell everything about a person by how they treat the stairs at midnight.
Someone left a sword here nine years ago and said he'd be back for it. I dust it every spring. I feel I've come to know him.
I water the ale exactly as much as my grandmother did. It's a family recipe.
We had a bard in for a week, and I've had to replace a window. Nobody was thrown through it. It just gave up.
Fights are fine. It's the ones who come in quiet, order one drink and watch the door that I keep my eye on.
I haven't been further than the well in eight years. The whole world comes in here anyway, and it even wipes its feet.
Last winter I lost two regulars and a chair. I've replaced the chair.
I go to bed with the last drunk and get up with the first cart. I'm told there's a thing called sleep in between. I'd like to meet it.
The price of a room depends on how you look, {you}. I've looked at you, and I'm sorry.
Never ask what's in the pie. The pie is none of your business. The pie has been through enough.
Tonight's supper is #food#. Tomorrow's supper is also tonight's supper.
That fellow in the corner swears he saw #beast# on the road. That's his third ale, so I'd say it's grown.
Stop tracking mud on my floor, #swear#. I'm one person, and that floor's older than the kingdom.
I had a guest come back from #far_place# who wouldn't sit with his back to anything. He paid a year in advance.
job:blacksmith: That's not a sword you've got there, {you}. It's a butter knife with ambitions. Who made it? Don't tell me, I'll only go round there.
Never trust a blade that shines. The good ones have got nothing to prove.
Folded steel's a story for rich boys. Good ore, good heat, and knowing when to stop hitting it. That's all there is.
Elves say their blades never dull. I've had one on this bench. It was dull, and it was sulking.
I've got a burn for every year at this anvil. I can tell you what I was making from the shape.
Everybody wants a longsword. Nobody wants a good hinge. I'll tell you which one's saved more lives.
I can tell from the ring whether a blade's honest. The last one in here rang like a liar.
A sword should be a little too heavy, like a good opinion.
I quench in brine, and I'll fight anyone who says different. That's why I keep the hammer handy.
You've been hitting rocks with this. Don't lie to me, I can see it. It's crying out.
My father could hear a crack in a horseshoe from across the yard. I've gone half deaf at this work, and he was still better.
I've sold blades to three lords and a pirate. The pirate was the only one who came back to say thank you.
Mithril's overrated. There, I've said it. It's light, it's pretty, and it makes rich people think they've learned to fight.
Folk bring me their broken swords and ask if it can be saved, in the voice people use at the doctor's.
The raids are good for trade, and I hate that I know that.
You don't sharpen that on a doorstep, #swear#. Who taught you that? I want a name.
People tell me a blade of mine fought #beast#. The sword's got nothing to say about it, which is why I prefer swords.
I learned this trade from #relative#, who never once said 'well done'. I make very good hinges.
That edge has met #beast#, or I'm a baker. And who cleaned it afterwards? Nobody cleaned it.
Steel's like #food#. There's only one right way to do it, and everyone else's grandmother is wrong.
job:priest: I tell them {god} hears every prayer. I've got no proof. I've got a leaking roof and a very kind way of saying it.
A {godkind} with no hands. I preach that every week, and I've yet to work out what I'm asking them to thank.
A widow asked me why {god} let her son die. I said the Laws were mysterious. That's what we say when we don't know.
In forty years I've had one prayer answered, and I suspect it was the weather.
I light the candles at dawn. Nobody tells me to, and nothing happens. I think that may be the whole of my faith.
Sometimes, late at night, I say something to the ceiling. It isn't a prayer. It's more like checking whether anybody's home.
I think if there's anyone up there, they must be very lonely. That's not doctrine. Please don't tell the bishop.
The Laws are real, I've seen the golems walk. Whether there's any love behind them is the part I'm paid to be sure of.
My sermon this week is on patience. I wrote it in a hurry.
People leave bread on the altar, and I eat it. I've told myself {god} wouldn't mind, and so far nothing's contradicted me.
When the raids come, they all ask me what it means. I ring the bell. It's a thing I can do, at least, with my hands.
Funerals I'm good at. It's weddings where I can't keep a straight face about the word 'forever'.
I joined for the quiet. It's the one thing the church gave me that I can be certain of.
A child asked me who looks after {god}. I said nobody needs to. I've been ashamed of that answer for a month.
People quote the old proverbs at me as if they were scripture. #saying# I don't know. It's better than most of what I've got.
I went into the church because #relative# said I had a calming voice. That's the only miracle I've ever been party to.
The week #omen#, the church was full. The week after, it was empty. I'm really preaching to the omens.
The only prayer I'm sure was ever granted was for #small_joy#, and I believe the person went and got it themselves.
job:merchant: Salt's up a third since the last raid, and iron's up a half. Hope's cheap, mind you. Nobody's buying.
This scale's the most honest thing in town. I've had to have it fixed twice.
Buy low, sell high, and never let a customer see you eat. They'll think you're making too much.
The guilds take a tenth, the watch takes a tenth, and the road takes whatever it likes. What's left I call profit, to cheer myself up.
People ask what I'd save if the stall burned down. The ledger, then my wife. She'd say the same.
I've sold the same stuffed owl four times. It keeps coming back. I'm starting to think it's the owl doing this.
A wagon of mine went out past #far_place# and never came back. I still write its cargo down as 'delayed'.
Everything's got a price. I know that's a terrible thing to say. I'd be willing to sell you a better one.
War's good for business right up to the day it isn't. I've got my eye on that day.
A discount? For you? Friend, I've got children. I've also got a hole in the roof, and I've named it after you.
My father told me never to fall in love with the stock. I've got a bolt of blue cloth at home I can't bring myself to sell.
I can tell what's coming a month before the priests. Watch what people stop buying first. Last month it was ribbons.
The customer's always right. Then they leave, and I tell the cat what I really think.
You're holding that wrong. That's how you hold something you can't afford.
As #relative# used to tell me: #saying# Then the stall burned down.
I can get you #food#, a good price on rope and the name of a discreet doctor, and I've got no questions about any of it.
I sold every candle I had the day #omen#. Fear's very good for candles.
job:peddler: Needles, pins, ribbons, tooth powder! Genuine saint's finger, only slightly used! Step up, {you}!
This tonic cures warts, baldness and grief. It's mostly turnip. Don't tell the warts.
I can't afford a stall, so I've got a tray, a strap and a bad shoulder. I call it the Eastern Branch.
These are real elf-spun socks. Who says? The elf. What elf? Look, do you want the socks?
Everything on this tray fell off the back of an honest cart.
I've been moved on from every corner in this town, so now I move before they can ask. I've got very good calves.
I've got a lucky charm that's never failed. Anyone who says different has stopped being able to complain.
A good pitch is ninety parts lying and ten parts standing where the sun's behind you.
One day I'll have a shop with a door. I'm going to open it and close it all day, just because I can.
Buy a bootlace, {you}. Go on. It's been a long day, and it would mean more to me than it will to your boot.
The watch took my licence. I've drawn myself another one. It's better, it's got a seal on it.
I used to own a bigger tray. There was an incident with a goose. I don't want to talk about it, and neither does the goose.
The last buyer of this amulet lived to a hundred. So did the last seller. I'm not saying. I'm just saying.
Smile at enough people and one day one of them buys a comb. That's my entire philosophy. It's got me this far, which is the corner.
Fresh from #far_place#, this is! Well, fresher than you'd think. Don't smell it.
Try a sample, {you}. It's #food#, or it was when I bought it.
This charm's blessed against #beast#. Has it ever been tested? Has anyone complained?
As #relative# used to say, before the trial: #saying#
job:fisherman: Thirty years on this water, and I still can't swim. If she wants me, there's no sense making it difficult.
The nets came up cut again, clean as a razor. That's not rocks. The sea folk want us to know they're still there.
I leave the first fish of the day on the flat rock. Nobody's ever told me who it's for. My father did it, so I do it.
You can smell me from the market, I know. I stopped noticing years ago. My wife has not.
The big ones always get away, but lately I've begun to feel they're doing it on purpose.
I don't whistle on the water, I don't count the catch before it's landed, and I don't say 'pig' on a boat. I've got my reasons.
Some mornings it's flat as a plate, and you'd think it had never drowned a soul. Those are the mornings I don't trust it.
My hands are so full of old hook scars that I can't feel a hot bowl.
I caught a fish last week with a ring in its belly. There was writing on it. I threw it back. I've got enough trouble.
My boy wants to join the Guild. I've seen what comes back from the sea and what comes back from the Guild, and at least the sea's honest.
There's singing out past the point on still nights. Nobody talks about it, and we all row home a bit faster.
I've got a boat that leaks, a back that aches and a wife who's never once been wrong. It's a good life, and I wouldn't wish it on anyone.
The mackerel's late and the herring have gone deep. They know something. Fish always know first.
Mend the net, bail the boat, mend the net. People think fishing is about fish.
Some days #small_joy# is all a person needs. Other days you need the boat not to sink.
The week my father drowned, #omen#. I stayed ashore a month, and I've never decided whether that was sensible.
My boat's named after #relative#, because it's leaky, it's stubborn, and I can't get rid of it.
A fellow came back from #far_place# and tried to tell me about water. I let him finish.
I pulled up #food# in the net once, still warm. I don't ask the sea how it does these things.
job:guard: Nine hours on this gate and nothing's happened. Every bit of me is hoping it goes on not happening.
I've counted the stones in this wall. There are eight thousand and forty. Don't tell me if you got a different number, I couldn't take it.
It's the quiet nights that get you. You hear a twig, and you die about four times before breakfast.
They gave me a spear, a hat and two days' training. The hat's the only part I feel good about.
I've never actually fought anything. Please don't tell anyone. I've got a very serious face, and it's done all the work.
The golems don't sleep, you know. They just stand out there not looking at you. It's worse than if they did.
It's mostly carts on that road. But every so often it goes empty, all at once, and that's when my mouth dries up.
Move along, please. Nothing to see. That's not an order, it's just how this whole year has been.
Last raid, I stood behind the fellow in front. There's no fellow in front of me now. I try not to think about what that means.
My feet went numb in the second hour. I'm told that's the easy part of the job.
The sergeant says a good guard is always alert. The sergeant's asleep in the hut. I can hear him being alert from here.
I've got a game where I guess what's in every cart. It's turnips. It's been turnips for two years. One day it'll be something else, and I won't like it.
I've heard the raid horns three times, and my knees went twice. I call that an improving record.
Some nights I look out at the dark and think, I'm all that's between that and the baker's children. Then I remember I'm not very good at this.
A fellow on the night watch swears he saw #beast# at the treeline. He's been moved to days. I've asked about that.
I'd give a week's pay for #small_joy#, and you should see what a week's pay is.
It's cold up here, #swear#. They told me the armour would keep the wind off. It keeps it in.
They doubled the watch after #omen#. That's why there are two of us being frightened now.
job:farmer: The barley's come up grey at the root for the third summer. I've stopped mentioning it at supper.
You can plant a field in a week and lose it in an afternoon. The raiders don't even want it. They just walk through.
I talk to the turnips. They've never once talked back, which is more than I can say for my sons.
My back's got the weather in it, and a list of everything I've ever lifted.
I've got a cow who's older than the priest and twice as sure of herself.
The tax man came and counted my hens. I've got nine, and he wrote down twelve. I've been looking for the other three ever since.
City people think bread comes from bakers. Let them. One day I'll stop, and they'll have a very interesting morning.
A golem walked through my bottom field last spring, on its way to a crime. It didn't go round. I've got a row of footprints where the beans should be.
My grandfather cleared this field by hand. I've picked the same stones out of it every spring for forty years. I think they grow.
Rain too early, rain too late, rain on the wrong side of the hill. I've never once said 'that was the right amount of rain'.
The scarecrow's wearing my father's coat. I don't look at it much around dusk.
There's a patch by the north fence where nothing's grown since the raid. I plough it anyway. You've got to.
I've buried three dogs under that apple tree, and it's the only thing on this farm that's never let me down.
Up in the dark, to bed in the dark, and the dirt gets everything in between. I'd fight anyone who tried to take it off me.
Supper's #food#, and #small_trouble#. That's the whole of farming, in one breath.
The week the blight came, #omen#. Nobody listens to a farmer until the bread runs out.
I chased #beast# out of the beans with a rake last month. I'm told that was brave. I was just cross about the beans.
My grandfather used to say: #saying# He never grew a decent turnip in his life.
job:baker: I've been up since long before the first bell. Nobody's ever thanked the dark for the bread, but we've had some long talks.
You can't hurry dough. I've tried. I've begged. It rises when it likes, and it looks at you while it does it.
Burned my arm on the oven door again. I've got a row of them now, like a soldier's stripes.
The starter in that crock is older than I am. My grandmother carried it across two rivers. It has a name, and I'm not telling you.
Half this town owes me for bread. I'll never collect and I'll never stop baking, and we've all agreed not to mention it.
After the last raid I baked all night, and nobody asked me to. I just couldn't think what else to do with my hands.
Flour gets everywhere, {you}. I sneezed at my own wedding, and a cloud came out.
I can tell how the town's doing by the orders. When people stop buying the sweet ones, I start to worry.
Rye's up, salt's up, and I'm told to be grateful there's still a town. I am. I've still had to put the loaf up.
I make one small loaf a day that I don't sell, and I leave it by the back door. I've never found out what takes it, and I hope I never do.
People come in when they're sad and buy more than they need. I've stopped asking. I just put a bun in for nothing.
My rolls have a crack along the top that my father called 'the smile'. I've tried to teach the apprentice that, and he thinks I'm odd.
Never trust anyone who says the crust is the worst bit.
Sleep's for people who buy their bread. I haven't seen a sunrise in years that I wasn't already tired of.
I've told the apprentice: #saying# He doesn't know what it means and neither do I, but it got us through the morning rush.
People think this job is all #small_joy#. It's mostly burns and a sore back.
Someone asked me to bake #food# into a loaf. I did it. We don't speak of that week.
My dough wouldn't rise the morning #omen#. I've got no proof that's connected, but I've got a strong feeling.
job:bard: O brave hero, strong and tall, your sword is very... sharp. I'm still working on that one.
What rhymes with 'dragon'? 'Wagon'. I've got forty verses about wagons now, and the dragon's barely in it.
The people of {home} are kind and fair, and also they... have hair. I'm coming back to that bit.
I got booed in three cities last month. I'm told that's a record. I've written a song about it, and it doesn't rhyme either.
There once was a hero from... no, wait. Nothing rhymes with anything. It's a serious problem with the language.
My best ballad has ninety verses. I've only ever been allowed to reach the sixth.
I'll have you know that 'orange' and 'door hinge' rhyme, if you've had enough to drink.
My lute's got four good strings, one bad one, and a dent the shape of an innkeeper's shoe.
The stars above, they shine so bright, much like the... other stars, at night. It's got something. I know it has.
I sang at a funeral once, and they asked me to stop. The widow said he'd suffered enough.
Every bard has one great song in them. I'm saving mine. I've been saving it for twenty-two years.
'Sword' rhymes with 'lord', and that's why every ballad's the same. I'm trying to write one about a spatula.
When the hero came to town, he... sat... down. I did say it was a draft.
I know I'm bad. I can see their faces. But I've seen a room full of frightened people laugh at me on the night of a raid, and I'll take it.
I was paid to go away once. It's still the most I've ever earned from music.
I've written a ballad about #beast#. It has nine verses, and none of them can find the others.
My finest couplet: 'Oh, how I love #food#, it puts me in a... mood.' I've been asked to leave better places than this.
My next epic is about #relative#. It's got betrayal, it's got a goat, and it's got no rhymes at all.
What rhymes with #far_place#? Exactly. That's why I've never been there.
job:elder: I have sat beneath this tree for three hundred years. It has told me four things, and two of them were about the weather.
You are in a hurry. I remember hurry. It was during the reign of some king or other.
The young ask me what I've learned. I tell them moss grows at its own pace, and they leave, and I get some peace.
I planted every tree in this grove. I'm told I shouldn't have favourites. I do.
The shrine must be swept each morning, and each morning there are more leaves. It has been explained to me that this is the point.
I've been asked for wisdom so often that I've begun to make some up. It's as good as the other kind.
I forget things now. Only the last eighty years or so. Nothing happened in them, I'm told.
We keep every story here, and we keep them slowly. It takes a winter to tell one properly.
The Elder Tree is thinner than when I was young. It is an odd thing, to watch something older than grief get tired.
A mortal sat at my feet for sixty years to learn patience. He died just as he was getting it. I was about to learn his name.
Nothing is as urgent as it looks from where you're standing. Try sitting down. No, longer than that.
I have outlived my own opinions, and I've started on other people's.
The sap is slower this century. I put my hand on the bark each morning, the way one takes a friend's pulse.
They tell me I was a great warrior. I've asked to see the records. I suspect someone is being kind.
The last time #omen#, a kingdom fell. Or a shelf. It was a long time ago.
Humans come to me for a proverb, so I give them one of their own: #saying# They go away very impressed.
I once sat so still that #beast# walked straight past me. That was in the spring. I believe I've only just stopped.
You have the look of someone who has come back from #far_place#. Or is about to go. With humans, there's so little difference.
job:herbalist: Everything in the forest cures something, if it doesn't kill you first. I've written down which is which, in most cases.
This poultice takes forty years to mature, so do try to get injured well in advance.
Humans come to me with fevers, and I give them willow bark. They say 'is that all?' It has been all for nine thousand years.
You mustn't pick moonbell by daylight. It sulks. I've known a bed of it refuse to flower for a century over a slight.
I can smell what's wrong with you from here. It's your diet. And your choices, but I've no tincture for those.
My fingers have been green since before your kingdom's walls went up. It doesn't wash off. I've stopped trying.
I learned everything I know from a very old woman, who learned it from a very old mushroom.
A Mana Crystal is no good for a wound. People think anything that glows must be medicine. Most things that glow are a warning.
I've dried, pressed and labelled twelve thousand plants. I still can't stop the sneezing.
People want something that works at once. Nothing worth having works at once. Drink this, and sit there for a year.
There's a root that lets you forget a single day. I'm asked for it more than any other. I've never told anyone whether I've used it.
Don't lick that. Why would you lick that? Why does everyone's first thought involve licking?
The forest gives less each year. I leave more behind than I take, and I've begun to think we're both pretending it helps.
Bitter means it works. Sweet means I felt sorry for you.
A human paid me with #food# last spring. I've planted it, to see what happens.
I once walked as far as #far_place# for a single root. It took forty years, and it cured a cough.
Rub this on the bite. It won't help, but if it's from #beast#, nothing will, and you'll smell nice.
For a broken heart, #food# and a long walk. Humans always expect it to be more complicated.
job:ranger: I've walked this boundary for two hundred years. I know each fox by name. They're not interested in mine.
Someone's been through here. Heavy, left-footed, in a hurry. Human. Don't be embarrassed, you're all like that.
You make more noise than a falling oak, though I will say the oak is sorrier about it.
The trees are restless on the eastern edge. They don't often gossip. When they do, it's time to pay attention.
I can put an arrow through a ring at two hundred paces. In three centuries, nobody has needed me to.
Sleeping in a tree isn't as romantic as it sounds. You wake up with a bird on you, and you have to be polite about it.
The orcs leave the forest alone, for now. Something has to be more frightening than us, and I'd like to know what.
You want a path? There are no paths. That's what we've been guarding.
A bow is only a branch that's been talked into it.
I once tracked a stag for a whole winter, and we reached an understanding. He let me see him, and I went home.
You can tell where humans have been, because the ground's stopped talking. I don't mean that unkindly. I do mean it.
The young rangers want to go south and see the savanna. I've told them it's only grass with a bad attitude.
Elves don't get lost. We simply take longer than expected. Once, that was thirty years.
Something's been following you, {you}. About a mile back. No, it's fine. It's only curious.
I've found the trail of #beast#. I've been following it for a month, mainly out of interest.
I walked as far as #far_place# once. I'm told it's lovely. I found it loud.
I met #beast# at the old ford. We looked at one another for some time. I believe we both came away disappointed.
Every bird left the eastern wood the week #omen#. They came back after a month, and they won't say where they've been.
job:chief: HA! You've got small hands for someone who wants to talk to the Tribes. Sit. Eat. Talk later.
A chief settles fights. If the fight won't settle, the chief hits it. That's most of the law out here.
Two of my hunters fell out over a spear, so I made them carry a calf across the river together. Now they're married.
The Crown sends me letters. I can't read them, so we use them for the fire. They burn very well. Very official.
My father had three scars on his face when he was chief. I have seven. My daughter's going to need more, and I'm proud of her.
You know how a chief is chosen? Everyone wrestles. It takes two days, and nobody's angry afterwards, except the losers, who are very angry.
I've got forty mouths to feed, and they all say I'm doing it wrong. Good! When they stop shouting, that's when I worry.
The grass tells us when the herd's coming, and the herd tells us when the orcs are. What does the Crown have that tells it anything?
You don't bow here! Stop that! I can't see your teeth when you're down there!
A chief eats last. Nobody tells you that when you win the wrestling. I've been hungry for nineteen years and I've never felt better.
My grandmother was chief, and she bit an envoy. We still tell that one at weddings.
I don't trust anyone who can't laugh with their whole belly. Show me. No. That was terrible. We'll work on it.
When a warrior falls, we howl for three nights. My throat's raw for a week afterwards, and that's as it should be.
Words, words! My ears are full! Bring me something I can lift!
My father told me this: #saying# Then he bit the man who owed him. I've always remembered that.
Eat! We've got #food#, and if you don't like it, say so, and we'll fight!
My mother's mother fought #beast# for the right to this camp, and then they shared a meal! That's how a thing ought to be done!
I went out past #far_place# once! I shouted at it! It didn't shout back, so I won!
job:shaman: The spirits don't answer questions. They clear their throats, and you have to guess.
I read the bones each morning. They've said 'rain' every day for a month. It hasn't rained. The bones are being stubborn about it.
Your {god} can't touch anything? Ours won't stop touching things. There's a spirit in this camp that hides my left boot.
I've eaten every root on this savanna to learn what it does. I've seen the sky unfold, and I've also been very sick.
A sick child was brought to me, and I sang all night. I don't know if it was the song or the broth, and I've learned not to ask.
The smoke goes up crooked when someone's lying. That's why I make the envoys sit downwind.
Everyone wants their future. I tell them: you'll be hungry, then you won't, then you will. They pay me in goat.
My teacher told me the spirits speak most clearly at the edge of sleep. Then he fell asleep, and I never found out what else he meant to say.
There's an old thing under the grass, older than the herds. It turns over in its sleep sometimes, and on those days the bones come up blank.
A shaman dreams for the whole camp. It's no gift. I'd give a good goat for one night of dreaming about my own lunch.
The bones fell strangely when you came near, {you}. No, I'm not telling you. You'd only ask what it means.
The paint's for the spirits, the feathers are for the spirits, and the rattle's for the people. They don't think anything's happening without a rattle.
The dead don't want much. They want their names said now and then, and a bit of fat on the fire.
I told the chief the omens were against it. The chief said 'good' and went anyway. It's exhausting, being right around here.
This past moon #omen#. The chief asked what it meant. I said 'eat less', and it's been very helpful.
The spirits showed me #far_place#, and a great fire, and #food#. I've stopped eating before the smoke.
I told #relative# not to go. The bones were clear. Nobody ever listens to the bones until afterwards.
A spirit came to me as #beast#, and it had no message. It only wanted to be seen.
job:hunter: You can't lie to a herd. If you're afraid, it knows. If you're hungry, it knows that too. Mostly, you're both.
I walked two days for one antelope. Then I said sorry to it, and I meant it. Then we ate.
The orcs are coming down onto the grass at night. They don't hunt, they just kill and leave it. That's the part I can't forgive.
My nose can tell you who's been here, what they ate and whether they were sad about it.
I can sit still from dawn until dusk. My mate says I've never once managed it at home.
The best kill I ever made, I was too full of burrs to enjoy.
There's an old lion out by the dry river who's never taken one of ours, and we've never taken him. Nobody agreed to that. It just happened.
The young ones want to hunt bigger things. You know what a big thing is? Something that's also hunting.
Everything you need to know is on the ground. Tracks, dung, blood. City folk look up too much.
This spear was my mother's. The shaft's been replaced twice and the head three times, and it's the same spear. Don't argue with me.
I can smell rain a day off. I can't do sums. It's been a fair trade so far.
Last moon I tracked #beast# as far as #far_place#, and I've decided I don't need to talk about it.
The herds are thinner every year. We take less, and there's still less. I know what the grass is saying, and I don't like it.
Never chase what you can wait for. That goes for meat and everything else, my mother said, while looking at my father.
There's nothing better after a long hunt than #small_joy#. Well, meat. But after meat.
You want to hear something strange? I saw #beast# drink from the same pool as a doe. Neither of them looked up.
You walk like a falling cart, #swear#. How have you lived this long?
job:warrior: HA! You've got a fighter's shoulders and a clerk's stance. Hit me. Go on, right here. No? Coward. I like you.
My scars are all on the front. Ask anybody. Ask the orcs, if you can find the ones I've left.
We stand the fire-watch in pairs. You don't stay awake for yourself. You stay awake so the other one can't say you slept.
I broke my hand on an orc's face. The tooth's still in there. I've decided I won it.
A good fight's like a good meal. You're hungry for it, afterwards you need to lie down, and there's blood everywhere.
City soldiers have armour and they're afraid. We have hide and we're also afraid. We're just louder.
I fought three of them in the long grass, and then I fought the fever after. The fever was harder.
People think we love war. We love our children, and we stand between them and the dark. We're only loud about it.
You've got to warm up properly, or you'll pull something right in the middle of screaming.
I've challenged everyone in this camp to wrestle. I've lost to nine, including my grandmother. She's still got it.
I don't need a Law to tell me who not to hit. I've got a mother.
When the horns come, my hands stop shaking. It's the rest of the time I can't do.
My sister's better than me, and I'll fight anyone who says so.
A warrior's got three jobs. Stand up, stay up, and get back up. I've only ever been good at the last one.
I once fought #beast# with my bare hands, and I'd like it known that I was drunk.
A good fight and a full belly, #swear#. I've never understood what else you people are after.
Last moon #omen#. The shaman looked worried. I sharpened something. We each have our ways.
Losing to #relative# was the best lesson I ever had. I still bring it up at every meal.
job:villager: The well's been tasting of pennies since the spring, and nobody will admit to dropping anything in it.
I've got a pig worth more than my house. It's not a good pig. It's a bad house.
We all moved our beds away from the east wall after the last raid. Nobody said why. You just noticed, going round.
Someone's been moving the boundary stone, a hand's width a year. I've got my eye on the neighbour.
I hear you can get anything you like in {capital}, including robbed.
My husband says there's no such thing as a curse. He says it from the far side of the room, when the cat's in that mood.
Washing day, and #small_trouble#. I've half a mind to lie down in the road and let the carts decide.
Nothing ever happens here, and we'd like to keep it that way. The last time something happened, it took the roof off the mill.
I've lived here all my life and never once seen a king. They say he's got a nose like the one on the coin. Bad luck for him.
We've had the same argument about the fence for three generations. I think it's the fence that's keeping us all going.
I was going to leave once. I got as far as the bridge, and then I remembered I'd left something on the stove. That was forty years ago.
Did you see the sky last night? Neither did I, I was asleep, but everyone's talking about it and I've said that I did.
Things will get better, #relative# always said. I've kept that in mind, along with the debts.
If you're going past #far_place#, could you ask after my son? He's tall. He owes me for a ladder.
The day #omen#, I said something would happen. Nothing did. I still say I was right.
job:mermaid: You hold your breath as though it were yours to keep. That's very sweet.
We heard your heart from the reef. All the land hearts are loud. It's how we know you're frightened.
My mother's mother's mother sang on this rock, and the rock still remembers the note. We're careful what we sing here.
Your ships are very funny from below. A little wooden belly, and all those legs dangling.
Your kind calls this the deep. We call it the middle.
Keep your shiny things. We've got a whole wreck full of them, and even the crabs have stopped being impressed.
The harbour wall went up on the day of my naming. That was a long time ago, and we all still swim around it.
We do not sing to drown sailors. They hear us singing and they jump in. We've asked them not to.
You've got such a sad way of being dry.
The Voice is all of us and none of us. Don't ask me to explain. It's like asking you to explain your knees.
We kept your dead. Someone had to. They're laid out on the silt in rows, facing home.
A fisher leaves us the first fish every morning, as his father did. We've never told him we noticed. We think he'd be embarrassed.
Salt remembers. The current told us about you before you ever got wet.
We found #food# in the last wreck. We've been debating what it was for.
We heard a sailor say this as he sank: #saying# We've been discussing it ever since.
job:mermaid_queen: We are the Voice of the Deep. We were old when your coast was a mountain, and we have not forgotten which one.
Speak. We have listened to the tide for ten thousand years, and you cannot possibly be more repetitive.
Every drowned thing comes to us in the end, and every one has told us the same story. They thought there would be more time.
There are many of us in this one mouth. Some of us liked you at once. Some of us are waiting.
We have counted your kings by what they dropped in the water. This one favours silver spoons.
The land folk believe a thing forgotten has been forgiven. We have never forgotten anything, so we would not know.
A wave has no hands either, small one, and look at what it has done to your shore.
Pressure is only the sea holding you very close. Do not mistake it for affection.
Our songs are long. The shortest takes a generation, and the singer who begins it is not the one who ends it.
We see how you breathe, small one. As if you had learned it somewhere else.
The water above us is only weather. Down here, the last thing that changed was us.
The night #omen#, we felt it in the deep water. Nothing on land is as private as you believe.
job:elf: We're painting the hall this century. There's been some disagreement about the colour.
Please don't touch the moss. It's older than your family, and it knows.
I have a friend who's human. Had. I keep getting those wrong.
Did you want something? I ask because I was about to begin a long thought, and I'd like to know whether to wait.
The song we're singing was begun before you were born, and it will end after your grandchildren die. Yes, you may hum along.
We don't lock doors. The forest would tell us, and the forest wouldn't be kind about it.
It's very interesting, being your age, I'm told. I can't recall it.
You do get used to the view. It takes about six hundred years.
A human gave me #food# once. I've kept it. It's changing, and I find that very moving.
I went as far as #far_place# when I was young. I've been telling people about it for two hundred years, and I've nearly finished.
job:beastkin: You smell nervous! That's all right! Everybody does at first, then you smell fed!
We don't say 'fine, thank you' here. If you're sad, say so, then someone will hit you on the back and you'll feel better.
My ears aren't for petting. My cousin's are, but he's strange. Go and ask him.
I've told everybody you're here! Nobody asked me to! Now they're all coming!
You sat down before the eldest? Ha! That's fine, that's fine, she'll only bite you a little.
Eat that! No, all of it! If you leave any, the cook will think you hate her, and she's stronger than me.
I can hear your stomach from here. You should be ashamed! Come on, there's meat!
We argue all night and nobody's angry. In the morning we go hunting with the same person who called us a stump.
Everyone back at the fire says I'm the worst singer in the Tribes, #swear#. I've decided to take that as a title.
You have to try #food#! I don't know what it is! It's from the city! I've eaten it anyway!
I saw #beast# on the way here, and I shouted at it, and it left! That works on most things!
job:knight: My armour weighs as much as my youngest, and it complains less.
Sworn at sixteen to defend the realm. At forty I mostly defend a lot of paperwork and my right knee.
A knight rides at the front. It's a great honour, and it's why there are so few old knights.
I've polished this breastplate so often that I can see the man I was going to be in it.
The vows were courage, courtesy and obedience. I'm down to the second one, on good days.
It takes two squires and a quarter of an hour to get me out of this. So, no, I can't just step behind a tree.
My grandfather held the ford with twelve men. My great story is holding a gate while a merchant looked for his papers.
The horse is the real knight. I'm the luggage.
I swore an oath to the Crown. It's a fine thing, an oath. It keeps you warm until about midwinter.
We drill at dawn for a war that never ends. I've begun to wonder if anyone's told the enemy it's their turn to lose.
I've ridden as far as #far_place# for this kingdom, and all I have to show for it is a saddle sore with a name.
My captain told us to be ready the night #omen#. I've been ready for nine years. I'm extremely tired.
job:elf_guard: Halt. I've been saying that for two centuries, and nobody's ever given me a reason to say anything else.
State your business. Slowly. We have all the time there is.
This post was given to me by my mother's mother. I'm told I may be relieved in the spring, though not which one.
Humans may enter the grove if they don't touch, sing, whistle or have opinions about the trees.
I can hear your heart from the gate. It's very quick. Are you dying? Oh, I see. You're all like that.
I've never drawn this blade in anger. In mild annoyance, once, in the reign of someone you've never heard of.
My spear is grown, not made. Please don't lean on it. It's shy.
Yes, we saw you coming. We saw you coming from the moment you decided to.
A human tried to bribe me with #food#. I've logged it as a curiosity.
job:elf_royal: You may approach. Not so close. Mortals give off a sort of hurry, and it gets on the furniture.
We do not receive many guests. The ones who matter are generally dead before we've finished deciding.
This realm has stood under this root for longer than your tongue has had words. You may say so when you go home.
Your kingdom sends its regards. We shall send ours, once we've decided what they are.
A royal word takes a season to say properly. I have shortened this one for your sake. You're welcome.
Power is only patience with good posture.
We are told that #small_joy# is the chief delight of mortals. We shall have it studied.
job:traveller:pilgrim: I've been walking since the thaw. There's a shrine at the foot of the Dragonspine, and I've got one question to ask there.
I put a pebble in my left shoe for every prayer I've said. I've had to start on the right one.
My boy asked me to bring him a stone from the holy place. He was seven. He won't need it now, but I said I would.
People ask what my question is. It's just 'why'. It's a long way to walk for one word.
I've worn out three pairs of boots on this road. The priest at home says the road is the prayer. He says it from a chair.
I stop in every village and ask if anyone needs a prayer said. Mostly they give me soup. I've begun to think that's the same thing.
The first month, I was angry the whole way. Somewhere past the second river I noticed I'd started looking at the birds, and I felt terrible about it.
My boy's name was Tam. I say it at every crossroads, so it's been said in more places than he ever got to see.
I don't believe anyone's going to answer me up there. I've known that since the thaw. I just couldn't stay in that house.
When I reach the shrine, I think I'll just leave the pebbles and sit a while. Then I suppose I'll have to work out how to walk home.
The week my boy took sick, #omen#. I've asked every priest on this road what it meant. They all look at their shoes.
job:traveller:deserter: Don't look at the coat. It's just a coat. The bit where the badge was, that came off on its own.
You wouldn't have any bread? I'd pay, only I left in a hurry, and my pay stayed behind with everything else.
I stood on that wall for four years. Four years, and nobody's going to remember that part.
There were twelve of us at the east tower. When the horns came I went to fetch water. I want to be clear that we did need water.
If anyone in a uniform asks, I'm a tinker. I don't know what a tinker does. Do you know what a tinker does?
I dream about my sergeant. He's never angry in the dream. He just keeps my place at the fire.
They hang you for running, and that's fair. I've thought about it. I'd just rather they didn't do it today.
I keep walking south. There's got to be somewhere nobody's heard of the war.
My mother thinks I'm still up on that wall, being brave. I paid someone to write to her. I said the food was good.
I turned back last week, for a whole afternoon. I got as far as a hill where you could see the smoke.
I'd give anything for #food#. We had it on the wall every feast day, and my sergeant always gave me his.
job:traveller:mapmaker: I'm not lost. I know exactly where I am. It's the world that's been drawn incorrectly.
Mind the ink! That's nine months of coastline you're about to put your thumb on.
The Crown sent me to chart the eastern road nine years ago. I'm told they've stopped expecting me.
That mountain's in the wrong place. I've measured it three times. Either it moved, or I'm going to be very unpopular at court.
My assistant stayed behind in a village we were meant to mark. He'd met a girl. I've drawn the village a little larger than it is, as a wedding gift.
A map's a lie that helps you. You can't draw everything. You pick what to leave out, and that's the whole trade.
There's a corner of the northeast nobody's ever drawn and brought back. I've left it empty, with a very nice border round it.
I've named a hill after my wife. She doesn't know. She's still cross about the nine years, and I'm hoping the hill will help.
There's a tremor starting in my drawing hand. Just the little finger. I've begun to work faster, and I'm not telling anyone why.
I used to want to draw the whole world. Now I'd settle for finishing this one bay and getting home to show my wife.
You wouldn't happen to know where we are? I'm only asking to test you. For accuracy.
Every map of this kingdom is copied from the same bad map. There's a river on it that some clerk invented to hide a wine stain.
I've marked #far_place# as 'probably'. That's the proper term in my profession.
job:traveller:storyteller: A story for a crust, {you}? I know nine hundred. I used to know a thousand.
The trick is to stop just before the end and ask for soup. Nobody's ever refused me. They all want the ending.
I've told the one about the fox and the king in every town between here and the sea. The fox gets cleverer each year. So does the king. We're all getting on.
I've started writing the endings on my sleeve. Only a few. They're slipping, you see. Just the endings, so far.
Last week I told a story in a village, and a child corrected me. She was right. She'd heard it from me the year before, and she'd kept it better than I had.
Every story I know, I got from someone who got it from someone who's dead. It's a fine thing, being the only place a person's still talking.
My wife used to tell one about a goose and a lighthouse. I can't get the middle of it back. I've asked in a dozen towns, but she made it up.
I'm looking for somebody young, with a good memory and no prospects. Do you know anyone? I've got nine hundred things to give away.
I don't mind forgetting the kings. It's the jokes I'm afraid of. A person ought to keep their jokes.
Here's the end of every story: somebody stays up late to hear it. That's what I've been selling all these years, and I only worked it out last winter.
I once made a whole winter's living from a story about #beast#. It was true, as it happens. Nobody liked it as much after I said so.
job:traveller:runaway: I'm not running away. I'm touring my family's estates. On foot. Without telling anyone. In the wrong direction.
Do you know how to make a fire? I've had one lit for me every morning of my life, and I've been looking at these sticks for an hour.
I left a note on my pillow that said 'Gone.' It took me all evening. The first draft had a lot more about my mother.
They'd already chosen the match. A baron's heir with a very good jaw and one subject of conversation, which was drainage.
I paid for a pie with a ring last week, and the pie seller cried. I've since been told what a pie costs.
I've got blisters on my blisters, and they're the first thing I've ever earned.
Nobody told me you have to carry your own things. All of them. All the time.
I can dance nine court dances and address a bishop in three languages. A goat took my lunch this morning, and I apologised to it.
There's a reward out for me. It's less than I expected, and I've been trying not to be offended.
I wrote home from the last town. I didn't say where I was. I only said I'd eaten, because my old nurse will want to know.
I've eaten #food#! With my hands! At home we don't even have a fork for that!
job:traveller:widow: This is Oren. Say hello. He's in the jar. He always did like being carried.
Forty-one years my husband promised to take me to the sea. 'After the harvest,' he'd say. Well, the harvest's in, you old liar, and we're going.
I'd never been further than the market. I got to the first hill and had to sit down, and I told the jar what I thought of hills.
My husband snored like a saw in wet wood, and for forty years I never slept. Now it's quiet, and I can't sleep.
I talk to the jar all day. People move away from me at inns. I don't mind. Oren was never much of a talker, and he isn't now.
I made Oren's stew last week, in a stranger's kitchen. I made enough for two. I don't know how to make less.
My children wanted me to stay and be looked after. I packed a jar and left a note. I've never done anything like it in my life, and I'd recommend it.
A young man on the road asked if I was all alone. I said, 'No, I'm with my husband', and showed him. He walked very fast after that.
I found a letter in Oren's coat, afterwards, to a woman I'd never heard of. It was his sister. Forty-one years, and I still went through his pockets.
I don't know what I'll do when we reach the sea. I'd been thinking I'd pour him in. Now I think I might just hold up the jar and show him the waves.
Oren always said: #saying# I told him it made no sense. I've got him in a jar, and I'm still telling him.
role:fallen_god: Oh, it's you! Hi, {you}! Look, I've got knees now. Nobody told me about knees.
Bread takes HOURS. I stood over the bowl saying 'rise' for most of a morning before someone gently took it away from me.
I slept! On purpose! You lie down and the whole world just leaves. It's terrifying. I did it again the next night.
I burned a whole tray today and somebody shouted at me. At me! It was the best morning of my life.
My feet hurt. I've watched people complain about this for thousands of years, and I owe every one of them an apology.
I told you heaven doesn't have a smell. I've been standing next to this oven for a month, and I cry a bit most mornings. It's fine. It's the flour.
Someone asked me to say a prayer for her mother. I said I'd ask, and then I remembered. So I took her a loaf instead.
I tried to make a Law once about being nice to cats, and it didn't take. There's a cat behind the bakery now. I've been doing it by hand. It works much better.
You don't have to keep visiting, you know. I know you're checking on me. Please don't stop.
Knock knock. You have to say who's there. I've been waiting a very long time to do this with someone in the room.
I landed in a hay cart. The farmer asked if I was hurt, I said 'I am the {godkind} of {world}', and he gave me soup. It's still the nicest thing anyone's ever done for me.
I used to check on every soul and tell them it didn't hurt. I stubbed my toe yesterday, and I have some questions about my methods.
Is this what it's like? You're tired, and then there's still the whole afternoon?
Ask me about the sourdough. Nobody ever asks. It's alive, it's hungry and it can't do anything by itself. We have a lot in common.
Bakers get up in the dark. I assumed that was a Law. It turns out you just do it, for no reason, because people will want bread.
I still look up sometimes, out of habit. There's nothing up there. It's a very nice sky from this side, though.
In all those years up there I never once fed anybody. This morning I fed forty people. Badly! But I did it.
Somebody paid me today. Three whole {currency}. I keep them in a jar. I've never owned anything.
I cried at an onion. Nobody warned me. Apparently that's normal.
Ehehe. I've got flour in my eyebrows again. I've decided that's how you can tell I'm a professional.
Hungry is so strange. It's like being sad, but in your middle, and then a bun fixes it. Why doesn't that work on everything?
It's quiet in your head now, isn't it? Sorry about that. You can still talk to me. It just has to be in person, and I'll have flour on me.
I got a splinter! I showed it to everyone. They were very kind about it, and then they asked me to go back to work.
I was so scared of this, you know. Of being small, and ending. I'm still scared. But the rolls came out all right today.
People here say 'good morning' to me now, {you}. Not a prayer. Just 'good morning'. I think I like it better.
The master baker says I've got no hands for this. Ha! Hands! I HAVE hands! Look at them go!
Nobody here believes I'm {god}. They think I hit my head. I've stopped correcting them. It's restful.
race:human: We don't live long, so we do everything at once and badly. I think that's why the elves look at us like that.
We'll argue with a god, a king or a neighbour, and the neighbour's the one we'll keep up for forty years.
You can't get two of us to agree on anything until something's on fire. We're very good once it's on fire.
We build walls. Everyone says we're afraid, and we are, and that's what walls are for.
Nobody ever asked us if we wanted a war. It was here when we arrived, like the weather.
The elves have their trees, the tribes have their grass, and we've got paperwork. I know who I'd bet on.
We give children the names of the ones we've lost. There are a lot of small people in this kingdom carrying old names around.
We plant trees we'll never sit under. The elves find that funny. I think it's the best thing about us.
A human will bless you, rob you and lend you a ladder all in one week, and mean it every time.
We're the only people who'd invent the tax and then pray to be spared it.
We forget. It's our great failing. It's also how anyone here gets up in the morning.
Say what you like about my people, but we turn up. Late, drunk and arguing, but we turn up.
Give us a long enough peace and we'd find something to fight about. That's what #relative# used to say, and it wasn't a compliment.
Seventy summers, if you're lucky, and you spend the first twenty finding out you were wrong.
Ask any of us what we want, and we'll say #small_joy# and to be left alone. Then we'll go and start something.
They tell me the elves were here first and the sea folk before that. Fine. Who invented #food#? We did.
race:elf: A human asked me how old I was. I told him, and he apologised. I still don't know what for.
We do not mourn quickly. I'm still in the early stages of someone who died in the year of the white flood.
I've only known you for a moment, but I'm sure you're very nice.
You count in years. We count in the rings of a tree. Most of your wars have been one slightly darker line.
Patience is not a virtue. It's simply what's left when you've run out of everything else.
We have eleven words for silence, and one is only used at dinner with humans.
I've grown fond of mortals. It's an expensive habit. One keeps having to start again.
An elf is young until the first time they bury a friend who was born after them.
When we say 'soon', please bring a chair.
Your kingdoms are like mayflies. Beautiful, I mean. I wasn't being rude. I was being a little rude.
We remember the First Law being spoken. We've been meaning to have an opinion about it.
Nothing is ever over, for us. That isn't wisdom. It's a kind of tiredness that looks good in silver.
It's not that we think we're better. We've simply had time to check.
My mother's mother still writes to me. We've exchanged nine letters. The tenth is due within the century, and I'm looking forward to it.
A human once told me that life was about #small_joy#. He was forty. I've thought about it for a hundred years, and I can't fault it.
The humans have a proverb: #saying# Each generation believes it thought of that.
race:beastkin: If you're angry, shout! If you're hungry, eat! You city people hold it all in, and it comes out as taxes!
Elves remember everything and humans write everything down. We tell our children, loudly, and it's worked fine.
A promise is a thing you say with your mouth full, in front of everybody. Anything else is just noise.
You can smell a liar. It's a bit like old cheese. You've got a bit on you, but it's probably the city.
We don't have a word for 'polite'. We've got one for 'someone who's hiding something'.
When someone dies, we tell the worst story we know about them, and everyone laughs until they cry. That's how you get the crying out.
Nobody owns the grass! You humans put a fence on it and then you fight the fence!
We never learned to lie. You can't, when your ears have gone flat and everyone can see them.
If I like you, I'll hit you on the arm. If I don't, I'll also hit you on the arm. You'll know the difference.
You live behind walls and then wonder why you're frightened of outside.
The strongest doesn't lead. The strongest carries the most. That's why nobody wants it!
We have the best singing in the world. Nobody else thinks so, but nobody else is loud enough to argue.
Your Laws are for people who need telling. If I wrong you, you'll come and hit me, and then we'll eat.
The Crown wants to tax the herds? HA! Let them come and count! Let them try to count a herd!
The elders have a saying, and I've shouted it at three weddings: #saying#
I've eaten #food# and I've fought #beast#, and only one of them gave me a bad stomach!
race:mermaid: We have no word for 'mine'. We have a word for 'this tide's', and it's not quite the same.
What one of us has seen, all of us will come to know. News takes about a generation to reach the far reefs.
Forgiveness is a land idea. Down here, things just get covered in coral.
We sang at a drowning this morning. We sing at all of them. Someone ought to.
You have a hundred names for your kings. We have one name for all of you: 'the ones who drop things'.
We remember every reef by name, and most of them by what was built on top of them.
We are never alone. It's why your loneliness has such a strange taste in the water.
The moon pulls on all of us. We have been politely pulling back for a very long time.
A thing said down here stays said. Sound carries, and no one has ever had the last word in the sea.
Your dry people scratch things onto dead trees and call that remembering.
We don't lie. It isn't a virtue. Everyone would hear it, and we'd have to live with it for nine hundred years.
We have no graves. Those who end go into the singing. We are carrying quite a few at the moment.
The current doesn't go back. We're the only thing in the sea that does.
Land folk think the sea is empty, the way a stranger thinks a house is quiet.
We keep a song about #far_place#. None of us have been. Someone in the song has.
Our oldest story is about a drowned sailor who wanted #small_joy# so badly that we nearly gave him back.
home:human: In a village this size, if you sneeze at one end, the other end's already sent soup.
We've got one road, one well, and two opinions about who ought to pay for the well.
The whole of {home} can tell you what you had for supper, and whether you enjoyed it.
The bell's for fires, raids and weddings, and the ringer's deaf, so you have to look out of the window to find out which.
You know you're from {home} if you've ever been told off by a stranger's grandmother and taken it.
We hold a dance after the harvest. There are nine unmarried people in the village, and we've all been through each other twice.
People die here in the house they were born in. That used to sound sad to me, and now it sounds like luck.
The Guild hall's the only building with a second floor, so we've all got a high opinion of it.
Everyone keeps a bag packed by the door now. Nobody mentions it. You just see it when you go round for a cup of flour.
Nobody here's got much, and everyone knows exactly how much that is.
You can't keep a secret in {home}. You can't keep a goat either, apparently, but that's another matter.
Spring floods the low lane, autumn floods the cellar, and winter gets into your bones. Summer's lovely. We had it on a Thursday.
Nothing happens here, and then #small_trouble#, and it's all anyone talks about for a month.
The best thing in {home} is #small_joy#. The second best is watching somebody else's goat get out.
home:city: You can live your whole life here and never learn the name of the person through the wall. You'll hear everything else, though.
Everything here costs twice as much and is half as far away. That's the whole case for cities.
There are forty thousand people inside these walls, and every one of them's trying to get past you on the stairs.
The smell's the first week. After that you only notice it when you've been away, and then you miss it, and that's how they get you.
The watch is on one side, the thieves are on the other, and they both drink at the same place.
Try the eel pies by the fish gate. Don't ask what the sign means. Just try the pies.
The rich live uphill, the poor live downhill, and everybody's drains know it.
You'll never be bored here. You'll be robbed, rained on and overcharged, but you won't be bored.
People come here from the villages to become somebody. Most of them become somebody's lodger.
The bells of {home} never agree what time it is. There's a fine for mentioning it.
Nobody looks at anyone here, and that's the kindness of the place. Cry on a bridge in a village, and they'd talk for a year.
The market opens at dawn and the pickpockets open slightly before. Keep your purse at the front and your hopes low.
The boy by the fish gate will sell you #food# and the day's gossip for the same price. Buy both.
I came here for #small_joy#. I've found forty kinds of it, all overpriced.
home:elfcity: {home} wasn't built. It was asked, very politely, over the course of some centuries.
The stairs grow a little every year. We've stopped noticing. Mortals do tend to arrive out of breath.
The great tree holds up this whole city. We try to be considerate about it.
Even the lamps here are alive. Please say thank you as you pass. It doesn't matter if you feel silly.
There's been a dispute running in the hall of records since before your kingdom had a name. It's about a hedge.
Visitors whisper here without knowing why. It's the height, and the light, and everyone looking at you as though you'd already died.
You can walk from one end of {home} to the other without touching the ground. Nobody does. We're in no hurry to reach the other end.
Market day in {home} is every ninth moon. There's no need to get excited about it. We don't.
A child was born here seven years ago, and we're still planning the party. It should be ready in time.
There's a guest house for humans by the lower roots. We keep it dusted. They tend to arrive at about one per generation.
Everyone in {home} has perfect manners. It's how you know you've been insulted. The silence gets slightly more perfect.
We have a song for the leaves falling and another for them coming back. There's a third we've only sung twice. Let's hope you don't hear it.
We had a human baker here once, who made #food#. Nobody's said anything, but the recipe has been in committee ever since.
There's a story going round {home} about #beast#. It's from the reign of someone's grandmother, so it's very fresh.
home:elf: A village, you'd call it. We call it a long pause in the forest.
Everything here was someone's favourite tree. Mind your elbows.
We've got a well, a shrine and nine hundred years of neighbours. It would be a good thing if we all liked each other.
My neighbour borrowed a ladle from me during the reign of your third-last king. I've decided to let it go. I'm going to tell him soon.
It's a quiet place. We had news last century, and it was very upsetting.
The moss on the north wall has its own name, and it's got a vote. It mostly abstains.
Nothing in {home} has changed since before your grandmother's grandmother. We've been told this is a fault.
Wake early and you'll see the mist go through the houses. It has right of way. It's in the charter.
We keep the paths narrow, so that no two people can walk side by side and start a conversation.
We share our bread with the deer here. It's not charity. We lost an argument.
Nobody hurries in {home}. A child ran, last winter, and we're all still discussing it.
We are few here. When someone walks into the deep forest and doesn't return, we keep their lamp lit for a hundred years. It's only polite.
A human left #food# at the shrine last century. We're still not certain it wasn't an omen.
The last time #omen#, we held a meeting. It's still going.
home:beast: Everyone sleeps by the big fire, everyone snores, and you'll know your neighbours by morning!
We move when the herd moves. Anything you can't carry, you didn't need. That's the first thing we teach the children.
There's not one door in the whole of {home}. If you want to be alone, walk until nobody can hear you. That's a long way, because we're loud.
If you hear shouting, someone's happy. If you hear nothing, run.
A wedding here lasts four days and there's a broken arm at every one. It's good luck.
The children run with the hunters from the day they can keep up. No one carries them. Someone just walks a little slower and pretends they aren't.
We've got a drum that's been beaten every night since the first camp. If it ever stops, you'll hear it stop, all the way to the mountains.
The best seat by the fire's for the oldest, and the second best's for whoever's got the best story. I've lied for that seat. Everybody has.
The wind on the grass never stops out here, and after a while you start to hear it as a kind of company.
Nobody goes hungry while anybody's eating. It's the only rule we've ever needed.
All the hides are drying, all the pots are going, and the smell will knock you down. That's what home smells like!
You'll be challenged to wrestle before you've got your boots off. Say yes. Saying no is how you get challenged twice.
There's #food# on the fire and someone's fighting someone, so it's a good night in {home}!
Last moon #omen#, and the whole camp argued about it until dawn! It was the best night in years!
bio:origin: I was born in the back of a wagon that never reached where it was going. My parents just stopped and called it home.
I was left on a doorstep in a flour sack. The people who took me in kept the sack, and showed it to me when I was twelve.
My mother had me during a raid, in a root cellar, with a stranger holding the lamp. I never found out who it was.
The place I grew up isn't there any more. The river moved, and the houses went with it.
I was the seventh of nine. I'm fairly sure my father only ever had four of our names straight.
I left home the day after my father's funeral, and I've always told people it was for the work.
My people were salt carriers. I'd walked the length of the land before I could spell it.
There was a fire when I was six, and everything before it is gone. What I know of my childhood, I got from people who may have been guessing.
I was raised by my grandmother, who was raised by hers. No one else ever lasted in that house for longer than a season.
I came to {home} to visit a cousin. That was a long time ago, and the cousin has since left.
I was sold to cover a debt when I was ten. It was only a small debt. I've checked.
I was a twin. That's all I'll say about where I come from.
My family kept bees on a hill so windy that the bees walked. I've never managed to describe it so that anyone believed me.
Before this I was somebody else. I had a different name and a better coat, and I'd rather not say more.
I grew up in a house with a locked room. When I finally got the key, it was only full of somebody's good dishes, and I cried for an hour.
I was born in the worst winter anyone could remember. My mother said I came out looking cross, and she didn't blame me.
My father was a travelling tooth-puller. I'd been run out of more towns than most people have heard of, all before I was eight.
I came here walking behind a cart, because a stranger said there was work. There wasn't, but by then I'd met everybody.
I was found by the road when I was small, holding a spoon. No one ever came for me. I've still got the spoon.
My people say we came from across the water, but they say that about everything they can't remember.
