I was meant to go into the family trade, which was lying to tax collectors. It's a good living. I broke my father's heart.
I grew up over a tavern, and I learned my numbers from the slate where they kept what people owed.
We moved nine times before I was grown, always at night. I was an adult before I understood why.
My mother was the only midwife for a day's walk, so I grew up knowing everybody's first secret.
I come from a family of gravediggers. We were never short of work, and nobody would ever eat with us.
The house I grew up in had a tree growing through it, and nobody ever considered doing anything about that.
I was raised in a temple, by people who were kind to me and wouldn't tell me why I'd been brought there.
I ran errands for a smuggler when I was small. I thought he was a very popular uncle.
My parents met on the day of a raid, hiding under the same cart. They spent forty years arguing about who got there first.
I was a sickly child, and people had stopped learning my name, just in case. I've outlived most of them, and I enjoy that.
I came to {home} with one bag and a lie about my age. The bag's gone, and the lie has held up very well.
I don't remember my mother's face, but I remember her hands on a loaf. I've gone looking for those hands in a lot of kitchens.
Where I was born, we buried the dead with their boots on, so they'd have a chance. I've never lived anywhere else that thought of it.
I was born the week #omen#. My mother said it explained a great deal.
Everything I know about where I'm from, I got from #relative#, and most of it was lies.
I come from somewhere out past #far_place#. You won't have heard of it. Nobody who stayed has heard of anywhere else.
I came to {home} running from #beast#. I've told it so many ways by now that I'm no longer sure myself.
I never set out to be the {job} here. I came for a week, somebody handed me something to hold, and I'm still holding it.
I was brought up on #food# and being told to be grateful. I've gone off both.
The first thing I remember is #relative# carrying me in out of the rain. The second is being put down, and I've never quite forgiven it.
I left home because #small_trouble#. That's what I told them, anyway. It wasn't that, of course.
bio:dream: I want to sit in a room where nobody needs anything from me, just once, until the light goes.
I'd like to be good at something nobody asked me to do. I've been thinking about the flute.
I'd like to see the far side of the sea. I don't know what's there. I suspect nobody does.
I want somebody to say 'that was well done' and then just stop there, without adding anything.
I've always wanted a garden with a wall round it, a gate I could lock, and one pear tree.
I want to go back to the last house I was happy in and knock on the door. I don't know what I'd say.
What I want is to be missed. Not a great deal. I'd just like somebody to look up at the door a few times.
Someday I'd like to sleep until I wake up on my own. I've never done it. I don't know what it's like.
I want to own one thing that's beautiful and of no use at all.
I want to dance at a wedding without anybody knowing who I am.
I'd love to write one letter that says what I actually mean. I know who it's for. I've got the first word.
I'd like to be the sort of person dogs walk up to. I've been practising.
I want to open a small place with six tables and no opinions, where people can sit and be left alone.
I'd like to hear my mother's voice again, once, saying something ordinary. Telling me to shut the door would do.
I want to walk out one morning in the wrong direction and not stop until nobody knows me.
What I'd really like is a quiet death, at a great age, in the middle of an argument I was winning.
I want to be forgiven by someone who doesn't know what I did.
I'd like to see my name on something that lasts. A bridge, perhaps. A very small bridge.
I want to find out what I'd have been if nobody had ever needed me to be useful.
I've always wanted to sing in front of people. I've got a terrible voice, and it doesn't make me want it any less.
I'd like one whole summer where nothing's on fire and nobody's dying, and I'd like to be bored by it.
I want to taste the snow on top of the Dragonspine. I saw a painting when I was small, and it's never let go of me.
I want a child to run at me the way they run at a favourite aunt. It doesn't have to be my own.
I'd like to be loved by someone who's seen the accounts.
I dream about a house with a door at the front and a door at the back, both open in summer, and a breeze going straight through.
Someday I want to tell the truth at supper, all of it, and see who's still sitting there when I've finished.
I'd like to meet whoever wrote my favourite song, and tell them what it did.
More than anything, I want to stop being angry with my father. He's been dead for ages. It's got very tiring.
I want to learn to swim. I've been afraid of water all my life, and I'd like to be able to say I went in.
I'd like to be brave, just once, with somebody watching. I've been brave in private, and it doesn't count for much.
I want to be an old person on a bench, telling lies to children. It's the only ambition I've ever been sure of.
I want to see what's past the place where the maps give up. Everybody says there's nothing there. That's what I want to see.
I want one friend who knew me when I was young. They've all gone, and there's nobody left to tell me I've changed.
All I want is #small_joy#, and nobody asking me for anything until noon.
I'd like to go and live somewhere past #far_place#, where nobody's heard of me or anyone I owe.
I want to cook #food# for everyone who was ever unkind to me, so well that they feel bad about it.
I'd give a lot to hear #relative# admit to being wrong, just once. It wouldn't have to be about anything important.
I'd like one more hour with #relative#. I'd only want to argue about something small.
I want to see #far_place# before I die. I've got no reason. It's the only thing I've ever wanted that wasn't for somebody else.
Someday I'd like to be the one who brings #food# to somebody who's crying. I've only ever been on the other end of that.
bio:fear: I'm afraid I've already had the best day of my life, and that I didn't notice.
I'm frightened of going the way my father went, slowly, calling everybody by the wrong name.
What scares me is dying while I still owe somebody an apology.
It's the horns, at night. I know it's usually just the wind now. My body doesn't know that.
Deep water. I've never told anyone, because people always ask why, and I can't say.
I worry that everyone's only being polite, and that they have been all along.
I'm scared I'm not a good person, and just haven't been tested yet.
I can't go into a cellar. Not since the raid. I send someone else and say it's my back.
What frightens me is how quickly a place forgets you. I've seen it done. It takes about a year.
Golems. I've done nothing wrong, and I cross the road anyway.
The quiet after everyone's gone to bed. I've been leaving a candle burning for years, and I tell people it's for the cat.
I'm afraid I'm turning into my mother. I said one of her sentences the other day, and I had to sit down.
I'm terrified of being a burden. I'd walk out into the snow first, and I've thought about what I'd wear.
I dread the day I stop being useful. I've seen what they do with an old horse.
I'm scared the war will end, and we'll all find out we've got nothing to say to one another.
Thunder. I know. Everyone laughs. I'm this old, and I still get under the table.
I'm afraid someone will find out I don't really know what I'm doing. I never have. I've been guessing since I was a child.
My worst fear is losing their faces. It's already started with the smaller details.
I think I broke a Law once, and I've never been sure which. Every time a golem turns its head, I feel it.
I'm frightened of being happy. Every time I've relaxed, something has happened, and I know that's foolish.
I can't bear being touched on the back of my neck. I don't know why. My body knows something I don't.
I'm afraid of dying somewhere nobody knows my name, and being buried as 'a traveller'.
Owls. You can laugh. Nobody's ever been able to tell me what they want.
What frightens me most is the thought that nobody's listening, and that every prayer anyone ever said has gone nowhere.
I'm afraid my children will remember me as I really was.
I fear the letter. I don't know which letter. There's always one coming, and when I see someone running up the road, my hands go cold.
I'm afraid I've been wrong about something enormous for so long that I couldn't bear to find out.
I'm afraid I'm getting used to it all. The raids, the smoke. I stepped over something on the road last month, and I didn't slow down.
I'm scared to go home. It's been too long, and I've told too many people how well I'm doing.
Mirrors. There's nothing mysterious about it. I just keep seeing someone much older than I feel, and they look so disappointed.
I'm afraid of needing help on a day when nobody's due to call.
I think there's something wrong with me, and I'm afraid the doctor would tell me what it is, so I don't go.
Fire. Not in a hearth. I mean the moment when it stops being yours.
I'm frightened of not waking up, so I always leave one small job undone for tomorrow. Death seems like the sort who'd respect a prior arrangement.
I've never got over the time I came face to face with #beast#. I still check under the bed, and I'm not a child.
I keep thinking about the time #omen#. Nothing came of it. That's what worries me. It's still coming.
I'm afraid I'll end up like #relative#, and I can't tell you why, because I promised.
I lie awake over small things. Tonight it's that #small_trouble#. It's never really about that.
I'm afraid of #far_place#. I've never been. I just know I don't want to die there, and I can't say how I know.
The night #omen#, I knew something was coming, and I went to bed anyway. I've been going to bed anyway ever since.
I can't look at #food# any more. It was the last thing I cooked for someone. I'd rather not say more.
bio:quirk: I count the stairs in every building I go into, and I can't sleep unless I know the number.
I apologise to furniture when I bump into it. I've done it in front of a duke.
I keep a list of everyone who's ever been rude to me. It's not for anything. I just like to keep it up to date.
I name the rats. I know I shouldn't. There's one called Margit, and she's been through a lot.
I can't eat anything that's touching something else on the plate. Stew is a daily struggle.
I always sit facing the door. I've done it for so long that I've forgotten what I was expecting.
I talk to my boots before a long walk. I tell them where we're going. It seems only fair.
I save the last bite of everything, and then sometimes I can't bring myself to eat it. It's a problem.
I can't pass a loose thread without pulling it. I've ruined two good coats and a friendship.
I sniff every letter before I open it. You can tell a lot. Bad news smells of lamp oil.
I pretend to be asleep when people come in, just to hear what they'll say. I've learned a great deal, and none of it has helped.
I hum when I'm lying. I've been told this by everybody I've ever lied to.
I carry a small stone in my pocket, and I squeeze it before I say anything important. It isn't magic. It's just a stone. I've had it for thirty years.
I leave one boot by the door pointing out and one pointing in. I don't know what it does. I've done it so long that I'm afraid to stop.
I say goodnight to the moon, out loud. It started as a joke, and then one night I forgot, and I felt terrible.
I write down strangers' dreams, if they'll tell me. I've got three books of them. I've no idea why.
I've got one lucky sock. I've never told anyone which. It hasn't got many good years left in it.
I make up life stories for people I pass. That one's a poisoner. That one's in love with a goose.
I can't sit down until I've checked under the chair. Nothing's ever been there. It's the 'ever' that worries me.
I always leave a little food on the plate, in case someone comes. Nobody's come. It's been a long time.
I knock twice on wood whenever someone says something hopeful. People have noticed, and they've stopped saying anything hopeful around me.
I collect buttons. I've got one from every person I've ever cared about, and they don't all know it.
I practise arguments in my head for days, with people who've no idea we're fighting. I win most of them.
I can tell you what day of the week any date fell on. No one has ever needed me to, and I've never stopped hoping.
I cut my bread into squares and eat the corners first. I tried to stop once, and I got the shakes.
I say 'bless you' to animals, trees, and once a door. I feel it's better to be safe.
I sleep with my boots on. You would too, if you'd seen what I've seen. Also, it's cold.
I keep a spare of everything, even when I can't afford the first one. I've got two bad hats.
I laugh at funerals. I can't help it, it comes up like hiccups. I've had to leave by the side door more than once.
When I'm introduced to someone I forget their name at once, and I spend the rest of my life avoiding it. There are people in {home} I've known for years.
I can't stand the sound of people eating apples. I ended a betrothal over it.
I go the long way round so as to pass one particular gate. There's nothing behind it. I just like that gate.
I keep every key I've ever been given. There are doors I'll never see again, and I've still got their keys in a tin.
I can't start the day without #food#, even when I'm ill, even when it's terrible. I ate it at a funeral once.
I keep a list of everything #relative# ever got wrong. It isn't spite. It's more of a hobby.
Before any long journey I say this out loud: #saying# I've no idea why. I got it from an old woman who was being chased at the time.
I'll walk a mile out of my way for #small_joy#. I've been late to two weddings and a hanging.
I always carry a bit of #food# in my pocket, for emergencies. I've been asked to leave two temples.
I've told the story of how I met #beast# so many times that I've started doing the voice.
I end every argument with this: #saying# It doesn't mean anything. It just makes people stop.
bio:secret: I can't read. I've been holding papers up and nodding at them for forty years, and I know the look of my own name.
I told everyone my brother died in the war. He didn't. He's alive somewhere, and he'd rather I was dead.
I was the one who left the gate unbarred that night. I've never told anyone. It was only for a moment, and I was going to come back.
I took money from a church box once, when I was very young and very hungry. I've been putting it back a coin at a time for thirty years.
I never loved the one I married. I was good to them, they never knew, and I've decided that's worth something.
There's a child in another town who has my eyes, and who's been told a different story.
I'm not who they think I am. The real {me} died on the road, and I took the name, the papers and the work.
I've been poisoning a neighbour's roses for nine years. I don't know why I started. They're beautiful, and it's been a great comfort to me.
I ran, the day of the raid. I ran past someone who was calling my name, and I tell people I never heard them.
I was paid to say I saw something I didn't see. Someone went away for it. I've still got the {currency}, and I can't spend it.
I don't believe in any of it. But I pray every night, in case someone up there is lonely.
I wrote the letter that broke up my sister's engagement. Everybody thinks it was a stranger.
When my father was dying he asked for me, and I said I was too busy. I wasn't busy. I sat in the next room.
I'm in love with somebody I've spoken to about twelve times. They've got no idea. I know how they take their tea.
I keep a bag packed under the bed. If I go, I won't tell anyone, and I won't be back. I've nearly done it twice.
I've got a small fortune buried where nobody will ever find it. I've never spent a coin. I just like knowing it's there when people are rude to me.
I once met a demon who was kind to me. It shared its fire on a cold night, and I've never been able to say that out loud.
I don't actually like children. I love mine, but I don't like children.
The story of how I got this scar is a lie. I fell over a goat. I've been telling people it was a wolf for twenty years.
I forged my own papers for this work. Nobody ever trained me. I'm very good at it, and that's the part I find funny.
I saw who did it. Everyone thinks it's a mystery. I see that person every day, and we say good morning.
I stopped believing in {god} the day I buried my child. I've gone to prayers every week since, so that nobody would know.
I've been writing letters to someone who's dead, and leaving them in a hollow tree. Last spring, one was answered.
I was married once before, to somebody else, in another place, and I've never got around to ending it.
I've got a sickness the doctor doesn't know about. I've got a year or two. I'd like things to go on as if I hadn't.
I broke a Law once with nobody to see, and nothing happened. I've been waiting for it ever since. I think the waiting is the punishment.
The best idea I ever had was stolen from someone who died before they could use it. Everyone thinks I'm clever.
I once let someone else take the blame for me, because they had a family to speak for them and I had nobody. They lost their place. I got it.
I send money to a family who don't know me. I owe them more than money, and they've got no idea why it comes.
I was relieved when my mother died. There. I loved her every day of my life, and I was relieved.
I've never once been as sure of anything as I sound. I practise the voice when I'm alone.
The dog didn't run away. I told the children it ran away. It's under the pear tree, and I go and talk to it.
I've still got a letter from someone who wanted to marry me, many years ago. I said no. I read it every year, on the day.
Sometimes I want to walk up to a golem and confess, just to have it over with. I've got as far as the gate.
I told everyone #relative# left me the money. Nobody left me the money. I don't want to talk about where it came from.
I once ran from #beast# and left a friend behind. I tell the story as if I'd been alone.
The day #omen#, I did something I've never told a soul. I think the two are connected, and I'm afraid to find out.
I've never liked #food#. I made one polite remark about it twenty years ago, and I've been eating it ever since.
I owe everything to #relative#, and I've told everyone I did it all myself.
I've been to #far_place#. I've told everyone I haven't. Something happened there, and someone I was with didn't come back.
I only pretended to be asleep the night #omen#. I heard everything.
bio:done: That's all of it, {you}. You now know more about me than my own family does.
There's no more, I'm afraid. I'm not that interesting, and you've had the best of it.
I've told you all I'm going to, and I'd thank you to keep it to yourself.
That's my whole life, then. It sounded longer when I was living it.
Nothing else to tell. Now you tell me something. No? I thought not.
You've got it all. Whatever's left, I've forgotten, and good riddance.
Some other time, maybe. You've had more out of me than most people get in a lifetime.
That's the lot. If I think of anything else, I'll make it up.
